title: Analytical Theory of Greedy Peeling for Bivariate Bicycle Codes and Two-Shot Streaming Decoding
summary: We present an analytical theory of greedy peeling decoding for bivariate bicycle (BB) codes under circuit-level noise. The deferred greedy decoder achieves 330x latency reduction over belief propagation (BP) at p = 10^{-3} while maintaining identical logical error rate. Our main theoretical contribution is a closed-form collision resolution factor A_0 = |true collisions| / |birthday collisions|, derived from XOR syndrome analysis with no free parameters, that quantifies the fraction of detector-sharing fault pairs genuinely blocking iterative peeling.
